title: Cohort retention-weighted HC budget & price sensitivity matrix
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is an operational budgeting tool that links cohort-level retention to headcount needs and price-elasticity scenarios. The goal is to produce a pragmatic set of hiring windows and runway impacts if hosted API pricing or commitment tiers shift +/- 10–30% or if cohort retention moves +/- 2–6 percentage points.

High-level approach (tabs):
- Assumptions: single pane for macro inputs (avg tokens/customer-month, avg revenue per token, gross margin assumptions, recruiter lead times, offer-to-accept rate).
- Cohorts: historical monthly cohorts (acquisition month) with retention rates, token usage trajectory, and revenue contribution.
- Hiring Plan: role-level templates (SWE2, SWE3, MLE, SRE, Solutions Eng), cost per hire (fully loaded), ramp schedule (months to full productivity), onboard risk buffers.
- Pricing Scenarios: up/down price moves across hosted/Dedicated/Private channels with elasticity factors per customer segment.
- Sensitivity Matrix: computed outcomes (net monthly margin delta, required HC delta, runway impact in months).
- Action Plan & Notes: bullets for exec ask, approvals, and tracked tickets.

Key assumptions (Assumptions tab):
- Base avg token consumption per active customer-month: 45k tokens.
- Base hosted API price (net to Redwood after credits/discounts): $0.0008 / token (weighted average).
- Dedicated effective price per token (post-commitment): $0.00055 / token.
- Private (on-prem) revenue recognized as license + ops: modeled as equivalent $/token of $0.00045 for long-term customers.
- Marginal gross margin at scale: 38% base (before pricing shock).
- Hiring lead time: 8 weeks to offer, 6 weeks notice, 4 weeks ramp = ~18 weeks to productive (use 4.5 months).
- Fully-loaded cost per senior SWE: $290k/year, mid SWE: $200k/year, MLE: $240k/year, SRE: $220k/year, Solutions Eng: $180k/year.
- Productivity conversion: 1 senior SWE ~ 1.4 mid SWE for token-cost optimization work.
- Retention sensitivity: cohort retention moves are modeled as absolute percentage pts (e.g., -4ppt means a cohort that was at 38% active at month+6 falls to 34%).

Cohorts tab (columns):
- CohortMonth | CustomersAcquired | Month0Tokens | Month1Retention | Month2Retention | ... | Month12Retention | TokensByMonth (calculated) | RevByMonth (calculated)
Example row (simplified):
- 2025-10 | 42 customers | 120M tokens total | M1 0.82 | M2 0.74 | ... | M12 0.18 | Tokens(month) = MonthRetention * Month0Tokens * customers

Elasticity modeling (Pricing Scenarios tab):
- Segment elasticities: PLG self-serve = -1.2, Midmarket (SMB) = -0.6, Enterprise = -0.25. These are applied to expected usage or churn depending on price move shape.
- Two behavioral channels: usage compression (customers keep but cut token usage) vs. churn (customers leave). We split elasticity 60/40 usage vs churn for PLG, 30/70 usage vs churn for Enterprise.
- Example calculation: Hosted price +20% -> PLG usage change = 1.2 * 20% = -24% usage; churn portion = 40% * -24% = -9.6% active customers.

Hiring Plan linkage: how we translate margin delta to headcount decisions
- Convert monthly margin delta into FTE-months using fully-loaded cost / 12. E.g., losing $120k/month ~ costs of 4.1 mid-SWE equivalents (120k/(200k/12)).
- Apply buffer policy: avoid hiring freezes unless net margin delta > 15% sustained for 3 months. Use staged gating: hiring freeze -> reprioritize non-customer-facing hires -> furlough contractors -> hard freeze 

Sensitivity Matrix outputs (Sensitivity tab):
- Rows = scenarios (price -30, -20, -10, 0, +10, +20, +30). Columns = net rev change month1, month3, month6; gross margin change; implied HC delta after 6 months; runway impact (months) given current cash and burn plan.
- Example scenario snippet (numbers illustrative):
  * Price -20% hosted (heterogeneous across customers): net rev change month3: -14% (mix shift to Dedicated/Private reduces loss to -9% by month6). Gross margin compression to 31%. Implied HC delta: -12 FTEs (mix: 60% infra/serving, 40% product/eng). Runway impact: +1.8 months (because faster savings) OR -2.6 months depending on committed expenses.

Actionable flags (auto-calculated tags per scenario):
- If implied HC delta > 8 -> flag for exec review.
- If margin < 30% -> flag for emergency cost review (includes cross-functional ops reductions).
- If churn risk concentrated in PLG cohorts (top decile), surface targeted retention experiments (promo credits, temporary slab).

Unresolved questions / items TODO:
- Validate elasticity numbers with Product → ask PD-analytics (ticket FIN-2345) to run two-week price A/B on non-core token SKU.
- Reconcile Dedicated migration lift assumptions with sales pipeline (linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cost-model/pull/87).
- Add region-specific GPU cost deltas for Q4 capacity planning (APAC cheaper spot reserves assumed).

Sensitivity table (short sample, from actual tab formulas):
- Scenario key: price_move_pct(hosted) | net_rev_delta_3m | gross_margin_3m | implied_hc_delta_6m | runway_delta_months
  - -30% | -22.6% | 26.9% | -22 | -3.9
  - -10% | -7.8% | 34.5% | -6 | -0.9
  - +10% | +8.1% | 40.8% | +4 | +0.6
  - +30% | +25.7% | 46.2% | +15 | +2.4

Quick conclusions for FYQ3 planning:
- Small price moves +/-10% have outsized PLG churn/usage effects; if we are considering sustained promotional credits, plan hiring gates for 2 quarters to avoid over-hiring into a lower-price environment.
- Dedicated/Private uptake is the largest lever to blunt hosted price pressure; invest in migration playbooks and Solutions Eng headcount to accelerate conversions. The model says each Solutions Eng pair accelerated conversion reduces net HC reductions by ~0.8 FTE in worst-case -20% price move.
- If we anticipate a -20% hosted price shock, require cross-team contingency plan: 1) pause non-critical hires (product infra), 2) accelerate Dedicated sales & targeted enterprise discounts, 3) test usage-preservation credits for top 30% cohorts.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally conservative on ramp times (we assume longer onboarding than org target). If recruiting cycle times improve, the implied HC deltas reduce by ~15% across scenarios.
- Spreadsheet contains hidden helper cells that map tokens -> GPU-hours -> spot cost (we should open that up in the next pass).

Linked tickets / references:
- FIN-2345: request to PD-analytics for elasticity validation (high priority)
- CONFLUENCE-1423: cost-model design spec (living doc)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cost-model/pull/87 (migration lift assumptions)

Immediate next steps (owner tags):
- Maya Chen: finalize scenario run with region-level GPU cost (due 2026-06-10).
- Arjun Patel: validate sales pipeline attachment rates for Dedicated conversions (FIN outreach) by 2026-06-04.
- Sofia Alvarez: sanity-check recruiter pipeline and revise hire lead times by 2026-06-08.

Notes about sheet hygiene: keep formulas in named ranges (monthly_rev, margin_pct, fte_month_cost). Add a pivot sheet for cohort concentration (top-decile revenue, churn-risk indicator).

If you open the sheet: top-left cell is a control panel with three dropdowns: Scenario (base / optimistic / pessimistic), Price move slider (-30 to +30), Retention shift slider (-6ppt to +6ppt). Use those to auto-populate the Sensitivity tab.
